== Biography ==

The Wizard, also called Mr. Wizard, is described as the same humbug Wizard as before, once known for mounting into the sky in a balloon; those he left behind waited for him to come down again.

During a journey with Dorothy, Zeb, Eureka, and the horse Jim, the Wizard obtained a plant whose leaves let the group walk upon water. He rubbed a leaf upon the soles of Dorothy's shoes and upon his own; Dorothy applied one to the kitten's paws, and the rest of the plant was used by Zeb on his own feet, on all four of Jim's hoofs, and on the buggy's tires. When an unseen pursuer warned them to reach the water or be lost, the Wizard drew the buggy down the bank and out upon the river, and once the buggy was in the middle of the stream he returned to the bank to assist Zeb and Jim, whose horse was plunging madly about with deep gashes on its flanks.

The Wizard was also counted among those empanelled as jurors for a trial, seated alongside the Cowardly Lion, the Hungry Tiger, Jim the Cab-horse, the Yellow Hen, the Scarecrow, Tik-tok the Machine Man, the Sawhorse, and Zeb of Hugson's Ranch. On another occasion, after the Princess's attendant reported that a closed door had been found open and that Dorothy's white kitten had crept out and run up the stairs, the Wizard and Dorothy exchanged startled glances, both remembering how often Eureka had longed to eat a piglet.

== Narrative role ==

The Wizard, also known as Mr. Wizard or The Wizard, arrives in the Land of the Mangaboos by balloon. There he faces the Sorcerer in a contest of magic, defeating him and, through the encounter, learning that the Mangaboos grow from bushes rather than being born.

Together with DOROTHY, the Wizard picks the ripe Royal Princess from the Royal Bush, and she deposes the Prince to become the new ruler of the Mangaboos. The new Princess spares Dorothy, Zeb, and the Wizard, but condemns Jim, Eureka, and the piglets to be driven into the Black Pit. The Wizard, Dorothy, and Zeb resist eating the invisibility-granting dama-fruit, learn they must cross toward Pyramid Mountain, and receive an offer of help from an unseen ally confronting the bear threat. The Wizard, Dorothy, Zeb, Jim, and Eureka then escape invisible bears in the Valley of Voe by rubbing magic leaves on their feet to walk on water. Later, the Wizard secretly gives the Tin Woodman a duplicate piglet, to be produced as proof of Eureka's innocence if she is convicted.

== Personality ==

The Wizard acts fast under threat. When bears threaten group in Valley of Voe, no hesitation — draws buggy "down the bank and out upon the broad river," leading Dorothy, Zeb, Jim to safety. Then goes back to bank himself to help Zeb and Jim, not staying safe in water. Protective instinct, puts others first.

Also quick with gratitude — cries "Thank you!" joyfully over small kindness (the leaf letting him walk water). But wary too: hearing kitten crept from supposedly-closed room, exchanges "startled" glance with Dorothy, both recalling Eureka's taste for piglets. Suspicious streak, quick to expect trouble even from those he knows.

Narration itself calls him "the same humbug Wizard as before" — frames him as trickster at heart, authority built on show rather than real power, even while acting brave and looking out for companions.

== Appearance ==

The Wizard is a small man with a bald head and wrinkled features. He is seen dressed in black velvet adorned with numerous sparkling emerald ornaments across his chest, an outfit that, paired with his aged look, makes him appear more amusing than imposing to those who meet him.

== Powers ==

The Wizard is repeatedly called "the same humbug Wizard as before," a description that frames his reputation as one of trickery rather than genuine magical power. Even so, he is shown wielding a strange plant whose leaves, rubbed on the soles of shoes and hoofs, let Dorothy, Zeb, Jim, and Eureka walk upon the surface of a river without sinking — a practical device he applies with evident skill under pressure rather than an ability inherent to himself.

== Relationships ==

'''[[DOROTHY]]''' — friend. Their bond seems close, as suggested by his recognition of her upon reuniting: "I am Oz, the Great and Terrible. Eh? And you are little Dorothy, from Kansas. I remember you very well."

'''[[Zeb]]''' — ally. Their cooperation is suggested by Zeb putting down the top of the buggy and inviting the Wizard to ride with them.

'''[[Eureka]]''' — friend. Their easy familiarity is suggested by an exchange concerning the kitten, in which the Wizard remarks, "if he planted you, he might grow some cat-tails."

'''[[Princess]]''' — acquaintance. Their meeting seems marked by deference, as the Wizard knelt and kissed her hand, crying, "We salute your Royal Highness!"

'''[[Prince]]''' — acquaintance. Their encounter seems edged with suspicion, as the Prince questioned him directly: "Sir, why are you here, in the Land of the Mangaboos?"

== Trivia ==

* Princess Ozma addresses him as '''Mr. Wizard''' when asking whether he named himself after the land of Oz or whether the land took its name from him.
* The foreword describing his return notes he comes back "just the same humbug Wizard as before," following an earlier ascent into the sky by balloon.
* He is named among the nine jurors Ozma convenes for a trial, seated alongside the Cowardly Lion, the Hungry Tiger, Jim the Cab-horse, the Yellow Hen, the Scarecrow, Tik-tok the Machine Man, the Sawhorse, and Zeb of Hugson's Ranch.
